subject: Business Models
title: The Liquidity Problem
description: A 60-second lesson on The Liquidity Problem.

hook.text: A marketplace with 100 sellers and 2 buyers is dead. The connection rate is nearly zero.

buildup.text: Liquidity means enough supply and demand for transactions to happen quickly and reliably.

discovery.text: Minimum viable liquidity: the point where enough buyers find what they want often enough to come back.

twist.text: Craigslist reached liquidity by being free. No fees meant sellers flooded in, which attracted buyers.

climax.text: Without liquidity, a marketplace is just an empty storefront. Nothing else matters until transactions flow.

punchline.text: No liquidity, no marketplace. Everything else is secondary.

quiz.question: What is marketplace liquidity?
options: The cash reserves of the company
Enough supply and demand for reliable transactions

details.summary: The liquidity problem is the biggest challenge for new marketplaces: without sellers, buyers do not come, and without buyers, sellers will not list..
details.whyItMatters: Liquidity determines whether a marketplace lives or dies. Solving it requires creative strategies like subsidizing one side, seeding supply manually, or constraining the market to build density..
takeaways: New marketplaces face a chicken-and-egg problem of attracting buyers and sellers
Most marketplace failures result from never achieving sufficient transaction liquidity
Strategies include subsidizing one side, manual supply seeding, and market constraint

faq.question: How do successful marketplaces solve the cold start problem?
faq.answer: Uber subsidized drivers with guaranteed earnings before riders existed. Airbnb manually listed Craigslist properties. OpenTable gave restaurants free software that also listed them on the marketplace..

faq.question: How do you know when a marketplace has achieved liquidity?
faq.answer: Key indicators include consistent match rates between buyer searches and available supply, declining time-to-transaction, organic growth without subsidies, acceptable fill rates for sellers, and repeat usage from both sides. Liquidity thresholds vary by category and geography.
